extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.

faqs.q: What is a skid-mounted 4-blade cement cutting bottle used for?
faqs.a: A cement cutting bottle is the skid-mounted station where big bags of cement are cut open and discharged during cementing unit charge operations. This one has a hopper, a 4-bladed needle that cuts the bag bottom, aeration nozzles and an air manifold, and a vent and discharge line.

faqs.q: How does the 4-blade needle in the skid-mounted 4-blade cement cutting bottle work?
faqs.a: The 4-bladed needle cuts the bottom of the cement bag so the contents fall into the hopper. Aeration nozzles and an air manifold then prevent self-weight compaction, so the cement discharges smoothly through the discharge line.

faqs.q: Why does the skid-mounted 4-blade cement cutting bottle have aeration nozzles?
faqs.a: The aeration nozzles and air manifold keep the cement fluidised and stop it compacting under its own weight, which would block the discharge. A vent line takes the displaced air and dust away from the operator.

faqs.q: How is the top valve on the skid-mounted 4-blade cement cutting bottle operated?
faqs.a: The top main butterfly valve is pneumatic-actuated as standard. Manual and electric-actuator variants are available, so choose from the air or power supply on the site and any hazardous-area classification.

faqs.q: What area classification options does the skid-mounted 4-blade cement cutting bottle have?
faqs.a: The listing offers ATEX Zone 2 and arctic winterization options. State the hazardous-area zone and ambient temperature range on the RFQ so the correct actuator and electrical equipment are fitted.

faqs.q: What does the skid-mounted 4-blade cement cutting bottle connect to?
faqs.a: Its discharge line feeds the cementing unit or mixing system, and the vent line goes to a dust collector. See [dust collectors](/c/cementing-dust-collector) and [cementing units](/c/cementing-units) for the connected equipment.

faqs.q: How does the skid-mounted 4-blade cement cutting bottle differ from a cement silo?
faqs.a: A cutting bottle handles cement delivered in big bags, while a [cement silo](/p/cement-silo-1-500-cu-ft-l-frame-aerated-load-cells) stores bulk cement delivered pneumatically. A site may use a cutting bottle for small jobs and silos for bulk storage.

faqs.q: Where is the skid-mounted 4-blade cement cutting bottle used?
faqs.a: It is used for cementing unit charge operations on well sites where cement arrives in big bags. A trailer-mounted version is available for in-field redeployment between locations.

faqs.q: How is a cement cutting bottle maintained?
faqs.a: Keep the aeration nozzles clear, inspect the cutting needle blades for wear and check the vent line and filter for blockage. Send the operating conditions through [our contact page](/contact) if you need spare blades or a service pack.

faqs.q: What should I send for a cement cutting bottle quotation?
faqs.a: Send the bag size and throughput, the top-valve actuation (pneumatic, manual or electric), the mounting (skid or trailer), the area classification and the ambient temperature range. Options are quoted to your specification.

faqs.q: Can the skid-mounted 4-blade cement cutting bottle be mounted on a trailer?
faqs.a: Yes, a trailer-mounted version is available for in-field redeployment. The standard unit is skid mounted, so choose by how often the unit moves between well sites.
